description: How to tell whether an intervention caused an outcome, from randomised experiments and A/B tests to observational designs such as matching, difference-in-differences and instrumental variables. Students simulate trials, compute power, estimate effects with code and probe the assumptions behind each design.
modelledOn: Hernan and Robins, Causal Inference: What If
Angrist and Pischke, Mostly Harmless Econometrics
Kohavi, Tang and Xu, Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments
Montgomery, Design and Analysis of Experiments
outcomes: Formulate a causal question as a target estimand using potential outcomes and state the assumptions needed to identify it.
Design, randomise and analyse an experiment, including blocking, clustering and noncompliance.
Calculate power and sample size and control error rates when many metrics or repeated looks are used.
Estimate treatment effects from observational data with matching, weighting, regression, difference-in-differences and instrumental variables.
Read a causal graph to choose adjustment sets and avoid collider and mediator bias.
Assess how sensitive a causal conclusion is to unmeasured confounding and report it honestly.

units.title: Causal questions and potential outcomes
topics: Association versus causation; Simpson's paradox with a worked example
The potential outcomes framework: Y(1), Y(0) and the fundamental problem of causal inference
Estimands: average treatment effect, effect on the treated, conditional effects; SUTVA and interference
Identification assumptions: ignorability, positivity and consistency
Framing a causal question: target population, treatment definition, outcome and time zero

units.title: Randomised experiments
topics: Randomisation schemes: complete, Bernoulli, stratified and blocked designs
Difference-in-means estimator, Neyman variance and the Fisher randomisation test
Cluster-randomised trials: intracluster correlation and the design effect
Noncompliance: intention-to-treat versus per-protocol; complier average causal effect
Factorial designs, main effects and interactions

units.title: A/B testing in practice
topics: Two-sample z and t tests for conversion and revenue metrics
Power, minimum detectable effect and sample-size calculation
Multiple testing: Bonferroni, Holm and false discovery rate control
Peeking, group-sequential tests and the sequential probability ratio test
Variance reduction with pre-experiment covariates (regression adjustment, CUPED)
Pitfalls: novelty effects, sample ratio mismatch and network interference

units.title: Observational studies and confounding
topics: Confounders, mediators and colliders; the structure of bias
Selection bias and survivorship bias in real datasets
Covariate balance, standardised mean differences and overlap plots
Bad controls: M-bias and conditioning on a collider
Case study: observational evidence on mobile-money training and smallholder income

units.title: Matching, weighting and regression adjustment
topics: Regression adjustment and the meaning of a coefficient as a causal effect
Propensity scores: logistic estimation, overlap and trimming
Matching: nearest neighbour, caliper and exact matching; balance checks
Inverse probability weighting and stabilised weights
Doubly robust estimation: augmented inverse probability weighting
Bootstrap standard errors for matched and weighted estimators

units.title: Quasi-experiments
topics: Difference-in-differences: the parallel-trends assumption and the two-by-two estimator
Event studies, pre-trend tests and staggered adoption
Instrumental variables: relevance, exclusion and the Wald estimator
Two-stage least squares and weak-instrument diagnostics
Regression discontinuity: sharp and fuzzy designs, bandwidth choice
Synthetic control for a single treated unit

units.title: Causal graphs
topics: Directed acyclic graphs, paths and d-separation
The back-door criterion and choosing an adjustment set
The front-door criterion and the do-operator
Testable implications of a graph and checking them in data
Mediation: direct and indirect effects

units.title: Heterogeneity, sensitivity and reporting
topics: Heterogeneous treatment effects: subgroup analysis and causal forests
Sensitivity to unmeasured confounding: the E-value and bounds
Placebo outcomes and negative-control tests
Pre-registration, reporting standards and honest communication of causal claims

schedule.title: Why correlation is not enough
schedule.exercise: Work through a two-group admissions or loan-approval table where pooled and group rates disagree, then write each unit's two potential outcomes and mark which one is missing.

tasks.title: Tabulate a two-group success table, compute pooled and stratified rates, and show how Simpson's paradox reverses the apparent winner
Simulate 1000 units with both potential outcomes known, reveal only one per unit, and compare the true effect with the naive difference in means
Build a simulation where treatment depends on a hidden health score and show how the naive estimate changes sign as selection strength increases

schedule.title: Estimands and identification
schedule.exercise: For three real questions (a school-feeding scheme, a mobile-money fee cut, a clinic reminder SMS) write the estimand, the population, the time zero and the assumptions that identify it.

tasks.title: Compute the ATE and the effect on the treated for a ten-unit table of both potential outcomes and explain why they differ
Simulate a design with a positivity violation and show with a covariate overlap histogram why effects for some groups cannot be estimated
Rewrite a vague business question as a precise estimand, then simulate an interference setting where one unit's treatment changes a neighbour's outcome and show the bias

schedule.title: Randomisation and the experimental estimator
schedule.exercise: Randomise 40 villages into treatment and control by complete and by blocked schemes, compare the balance achieved, and compute the difference in means with a confidence interval.

tasks.title: Randomise 40 units by complete, Bernoulli and blocked designs, repeat 500 times and compare how often each scheme leaves covariates imbalanced
Compute the difference in means and Neyman standard error for a small trial table and build the 95 percent confidence interval
Run a Fisher randomisation test by permuting labels 10000 times, then compare its p-value with the t-test on skewed outcome data

schedule.title: Clusters, compliance and factorial designs
schedule.exercise: A radio campaign is assigned by district but measured on households: compute the design effect, then analyse a trial where only 70 percent of those offered the treatment took it.

tasks.title: Compute the design effect for cluster sizes of 20 and ICC of 0.05, and the effective sample size of 60 clusters
Simulate noncompliance, estimate intention-to-treat and the complier effect with the Wald ratio, and verify the compliers' true effect
Analyse a 2x2 factorial trial of two messaging factors with regression, plot the interaction, and judge whether main effects can be interpreted alone

schedule.title: Tests, power and sample size
schedule.exercise: Size a conversion-rate test for a payments app: choose the baseline, the minimum detectable effect, alpha and power, then say what happens to the sample size if the effect is halved.

tasks.title: Run a two-proportion z-test on given conversion counts for two app variants and interpret the p-value and interval in plain words
Plot a power curve against sample size for a 10 percent baseline and find the sample needed to detect a one point lift at 80 percent power
Simulate 100 null metrics, count false positives with no correction, Bonferroni, Holm and false discovery rate control, and compare power on added true effects

schedule.title: Sequential testing, variance reduction and pitfalls
schedule.exercise: Review a screenshot-style report of an experiment that was stopped early and one with a sample ratio mismatch, and list what is wrong and what you would rerun.

tasks.title: Simulate an A/A test checked daily for 30 days and show the false positive rate inflating, then fix it with a group-sequential boundary
Reduce metric variance with a pre-experiment covariate, report the percent drop in standard error and the saving in required sample size
Detect a sample ratio mismatch with a chi-square test on given allocation counts and simulate a novelty effect that decays over weeks

schedule.title: Confounding, bias and bad controls
schedule.exercise: Using a survey of farmers who did and did not attend a mobile-money training, list likely confounders, draw the bias story, and decide which variables you would and would not adjust for.

tasks.title: Classify given variables in a small scenario as confounder, mediator or collider and compute stratum-specific effects to see which adjustment helps
Compute standardised mean differences before and after adjustment for a farmer-training dataset and draw a covariate balance plot
Simulate a collider structure, show that adjusting for it creates a spurious association, and compare it with the correct unadjusted estimate

schedule.title: Regression adjustment and propensity scores
schedule.exercise: Estimate the effect of a farm-extension visit on yield by regression, then by matching on a propensity score, and compare the two answers and their balance.

tasks.title: Fit a regression of yield on treatment and covariates, read the treatment coefficient as an effect, and compare it with the unadjusted difference
Estimate propensity scores by logistic regression and draw overlap histograms for treated and untreated units, trimming units outside common support
Do 1-to-1 nearest-neighbour matching with a caliper, check balance, and compare the matched estimate with the known true effect in simulated data

schedule.title: Weighting, doubly robust methods and uncertainty
schedule.exercise: Compute stabilised weights, check the effective sample size, and report a doubly robust estimate with a bootstrap interval for the extension-visit data.

tasks.title: Compute inverse probability weights for eight units from given propensity scores and the weighted treated and control means
Implement an augmented inverse probability weighting estimator and show it stays unbiased when only the outcome model or only the propensity model is correct
Bootstrap a matched estimate with 1000 resamples and compare the interval with the naive standard error to see why the latter is too narrow

schedule.title: Difference-in-differences
schedule.exercise: Evaluate a fuel-subsidy or mobile-money fee change that hit some regions first: draw the pre-trend plot, compute the two-by-two estimate and discuss threats to parallel trends.

tasks.title: Compute the two-by-two difference-in-differences estimate from four group means and sketch the counterfactual line on the trend plot
Fit an event-study regression on a panel with leads and lags and judge from the lead coefficients whether parallel trends is plausible
Simulate staggered adoption with effects that grow over time and show how a single two-way fixed-effects estimate misleads compared with cohort-specific estimates

schedule.title: Instruments, discontinuities and synthetic controls
schedule.exercise: Choose a valid instrument for a given question (distance to a school, a lottery), argue relevance and exclusion, and decide when a score cutoff supports a discontinuity design.

tasks.title: Compute the Wald estimator from the reduced-form and first-stage coefficients of a given lottery instrument and interpret it as an effect for compliers
Fit a local linear regression on both sides of a score cutoff, vary the bandwidth and plot how the estimated jump changes
Implement two-stage least squares, check the first-stage F-statistic with a weak instrument, and show the bias toward the OLS estimate

schedule.title: Causal graphs and identification
schedule.exercise: Draw a graph for a clinic-attendance study, list every back-door path from treatment to outcome, name a minimal adjustment set and test one implication of the graph in data.

tasks.title: Draw a six-variable causal graph and list every path from treatment to outcome with each path marked open or blocked given a conditioning set
Apply the back-door criterion to three given graphs and write the minimal adjustment set for each, justifying every excluded variable
Simulate data from a known graph, test the conditional independencies it implies with partial correlations, and detect the one edge that was wrongly omitted

schedule.title: Heterogeneity, sensitivity and honest reporting
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page causal report on an extension-visit evaluation: estimand, design, estimate, subgroup results, an E-value for hidden confounding and a limitations paragraph.

tasks.title: Compute the E-value for a risk ratio of 1.8 and state in words how strong an unmeasured confounder must be to explain it away
Estimate subgroup effects by region and age band with interaction terms and decide whether differences are real or consistent with chance
Run a negative-control outcome test on a matched study and show that a nonzero effect on the placebo outcome reveals residual confounding
